root.claim: One deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of tapes computes the exact $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit integers in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, disproving the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Schonhage and Strassen in this model.
root.method: Build two tape procedures (address-chunk interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers) whose volume-normalized costs save a power of their parameter through a finite linear network with a rank deficit, embed them in a chain of reductions from integer multiplication to convolution over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$, recover the exact product, and divide every cost by the volume $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$.

motivation.text: Scanning the $\Theta(n)$ stored bits once per transform level over $\Theta(\log n)$ levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so beating $n\log n$ requires saving on both data movement and butterfly arithmetic.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$. We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

children.claim: To refute the conjecture in the fixed-tape model it suffices to exhibit one machine $A$ with $\liminf_{n\to\infty}T_A(n)/(n\lg n)=0$, and a bound $T_A(n)=O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa>0$ makes this ratio tend to zero through all input lengths.

quote.quote: The power saving proved here gives a limit of zero through all input lengths, which is a stronger conclusion.

children.claim: Two tape procedures save a power of their parameter: interchanging two disjoint $u$-bit address fields costs $O(Vu^\tau)$, and a simultaneous normalized butterfly layer on at most $d$ chunks of polynomial records costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\tau,\lambda'<1$ fixed.
children.method: Derive both from fixed finite linear networks that exchange two banks while restoring scratch values and whose total edge rank $s$ is below $Wm$: run each network on row-split role streams of volume $V/W$ with frames, implement each edge change by smaller calls of the same procedure, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: Multiplying the parameter by $m$ multiplies the normalized recursive cost only by $s/W<m$, so the cost grows like a power of the parameter below one.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

children.claim: On a fixed number of tapes, arrays stored in lexicographic address order admit linear-time primitives: permuting or moving fixed-radix digits, splitting on a digit to apply a pointwise map and merging, dealing whole rows cyclically to $W$ streams, and cyclically shifting a target field by an offset computed from earlier fields, each in $O(V)$ steps.
children.method: Split the ordered stream on the relevant digits or at the shift offset and merge the pieces in the required order, charging counters and descriptor arithmetic to the scanned volume.

motivation.text: Addresses are implicit in positions, so moving one fixed-radix digit or rotating a field that follows its controls only splits and merges ordered streams a bounded number of times, unlike interchanging fields whose number of digits grows.

quote.quote: We distinguish moving one digit in a fixed radix, which needs a bounded number of scans, from interchanging fields whose numbers of digits grow.

children.claim: For a fixed radix $q\ge2$, permuting the digit values at two positions, moving one digit, splitting on a digit to apply a fixed pointwise map and merging, and dealing whole rows of $[P]\times[R]\times[B]$ cyclically into $W$ streams of volume $V/W$ each (merging back when $W$ divides $R$) all take $O(V)$ steps, counters and cleanup included.

quote.quote: Each of the following operations on an array of volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

children.claim: If a target field ranging over $[Q]$, with $Q$ a power of a fixed prime $q$, follows its control fields, the update $y\mapsto y+a(\text{controls})\bmod Q$ costs $O(V)$ by splitting each fiber at $Q-a$ and merging the two pieces in the opposite order, provided the offset takes time polynomial in $\log Q$; multiplication of the target by a fixed rational unit, and negation, also cost $O(V)$.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: Two fixed finite linear networks, a bit network over $\mathbb F_2$ and a complex network over $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, each exchange two banks of $N$ values with prescribed signs while restoring every scratch value, and carry nested subspace labels whose edge changes cost $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$ and $s_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$ smaller calls, so that $s/W<m^\tau$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Build the scalar exchange from three stages of eight-row invocations on three-element subsets of $[100]$, let frames on arrays commute with pointwise gates, attach tensor-product labels spanned by triple indicator vectors and count each edge's orthogonal residual, then realize the labels as rational projections (bit variant) or Hamming-weight phase frames (complex variant).

motivation.text: If labels only grow except on a few edges, the residual dimensions, which count the smaller calls, sum to $Wm$ minus a positive multiple of $N$, so the number of smaller calls falls strictly below $Wm$.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values a forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value unchanged, so a forward stage 1, an inverse stage 2 and a forward stage 3 send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ and restore every scratch wire; in the bit network this is the permutation exchanging $X_a$ and $Y_a$.
children.method: Run in each invocation an eight-row schedule of copy, gather, scatter and side-injection gates that first subtracts the effect of the old scratch values, then adds the source's effect, then restores the scratch, and check through intersection sizes that gather-scatter plus side injection has identity coefficients.

motivation.text: Rows dealt to scratch roles carry arbitrary data, so the exchange must hold and restore for every initial scratch value; subtracting the old scratch effect first makes the net change independent of it, and routing through $h$ central wires keeps the gather and scatter low-rank.

children.claim: At stage $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ the network fixes the other two coordinates of $a\in\mathcal T^3$ and runs one invocation on the $v$ values of each bank that vary coordinate $j$, so there are $v^2$ invocations per stage and $I=3v^2=78440670000$ in all, each with its own scratch wires: side wires $A_{ST}$ for neighbouring ordered pairs of triples and central wires $C_i$, $i\in[h]$, plus $C_\ast$ in the complex network.

quote.quote: Thus there are $v^2$ separate invocations at each stage.

children.claim: In the bit network (scalars in $\mathbb F_2$) triples $S,T$ are neighbours when $|S\cap T|=1$, copy adds $x_T$ to $A_{ST}$, side injection adds $\sum_{T:|S\cap T|=1}A_{ST}$ to $y_S$, gather adds $\sum_{T\ni i}x_T$ to $C_i$ and scatter adds $\sum_{i\in S}C_i$ to $y_S$; in the complex network (scalars in $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$) neighbours are distinct triples with even intersection, side injection adds $-\sum_T\frac{|S\cap T|-1}{2}A_{ST}$, gather also adds $\sum_Tx_T$ to $C_\ast$, and scatter adds $(\sum_{i\in S}C_i-C_\ast)/2$.

quote.quote: In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, and $S,T$ are neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$.

children.claim: A forward invocation runs eight rows, 0 subtract side injection, 1 subtract scatter, 2 copy, 3 gather, 4 scatter, 5 side injection, 6 undo gather, 7 undo copy: rows 0-1 remove the effect of the old scratch values, rows 2-5 introduce the source values and add their effect to the target, and rows 6-7 restore the scratch values.

quote.quote: the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.claim: With initial side and central vectors $a,c$, rows 0-1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$ from $y$, rows 2-3 change the scratch to $a+\mathcal Vx$ and $c+\mathcal Gx$, rows 4-5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$, and rows 6-7 restore $a,c$, so the net target change $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ does not depend on the scratch values.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: The net coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is the identity: in the bit network the central coefficient is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$ and the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one cases, while intersections zero and two already give zero and the self coefficient is one; in the complex network the central coefficient is $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$, the side wires cancel intersections zero and two, intersection one already gives zero, and the self coefficient is one.

quote.quote: Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: Since the inverse schedule with logical source $Y$ and target $X$ effects $X\gets X-Y$, the three stages send $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then to $(-y,y+x)$, then to $(-y,x)$, each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

quote.quote: $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: A triple has $z_{\rm b}=3\binom{97}{2}=13968$ neighbours in the bit network and $z_{\rm c}=\binom{97}{3}+3\cdot97=147731$ in the complex one, each invocation has $vz$ ordered side wires and $c_{\rm b}=100$ or $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires, so the wire counts are $W_{\rm b}=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})=177176569091445000000$ and $W_{\rm c}=2N+I(vz_{\rm c}+c_{\rm c})=1873807244643542670000$, fixed independently of the input length.

quote.quote: W_{\rm b}&=2N+I(vz_{\rm b}+c_{\rm b})

adds.meaning: The number $I=3v^2=78440670000$ of invocations over the three stages, each with its own scratch wires.

children.salient: The exchange is exact for arbitrary, unknown initial scratch values and returns each of them unchanged.

children.claim: If each scalar becomes an array on a common address set $\Omega$, each vertex $v$ gets an invertible frame $D_v$ shared by all incidences of a gate, and each edge $u\to v$ applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$, then linearity gives $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$, so the network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$ and a signed route $w\to\rho(w)$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ on every role, auxiliary roles included.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.salient: Only the two endpoint frames of a route matter: all intermediate frames cancel, so they can be chosen freely to make every edge cheap.

children.claim: Nondegenerate subspaces of $\mathcal F$ (dimension $m$) can label all sources, gates and sinks so that every edge joins nested labels and the absolute dimension changes sum to $Wm-2N+2L$ with $L=Ich$, where $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$ are both below $1/2$.
children.method: Pair triple indicator vectors by a form that makes neighbours orthogonal, prescribe the terminal labels, expose one tensor factor per stage, order the gates so that only the central wires' return loses dimension, and tabulate every edge's orthogonal residual.

motivation.text: Because neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal, side-wire labels can grow through nested subspaces, confining every loss of dimension to the central wires.

quote.quote: Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

children.claim: For the bit network $F=\mathbb Q^h$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=x^{\mathsf T}(I-J/9)y$ (eigenvalues $1$ and $-91/9$) gives $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, and for the complex network $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ with the dot product gives $t_T\cdot t_T=1$, so in both every triple line is nondegenerate and neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

children.claim: The terminal labels are $U_a\to\mathcal F$ on $X_a$, $0\to U_a^\perp$ on $Y_a$ and $0\to\mathcal F$ on every scratch role, so source dimensions sum to $N$, sink dimensions to $Wm-N$, gate contributions cancel, the signed changes sum to $Wm-2N$, and a total loss $L$ on decreasing edges makes the absolute sum $Wm-2N+2L$.

quote.quote: Thus the signed dimension changes will sum to $Wm-2N$, because the contributions at gates cancel.

children.claim: At stage $j$, with $A=F^{\otimes(j-1)}$, $P=\langle t_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_{j-1}}\rangle$, $B=P^\perp\subset A$ and $Q=\langle t_{a_{j+1}}\otimes\cdots\otimes t_{a_3}\rangle$, a data wire with triple indicator $t$ passes from $A\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $(A\otimes F)\otimes Q$ on $X$ and from $B\otimes\langle t\rangle\otimes Q$ to $((B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp))\otimes Q$ on $Y$, and with $A'=A\otimes F$ and $P'=P\otimes\langle t\rangle$ these are the next stage's incoming labels, starting at $U_a$ and $0$ and ending at $\mathcal F$ and $U_a^\perp$.

quote.quote: These transitions expose one tensor factor at each stage.

children.claim: With gates touching the wires in the order $Y$-side, $Y$-center, $X$-side, $X$-center, $Y$-center, $Y$-side, $X$-center, $X$-side, the common gate labels (tensored by $Q$) at times $0,\dots,7$ are $B\otimes\langle t\rangle$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes\langle t\rangle)$, $A\otimes F$, $B\otimes F$, $(B\otimes F)\perp(P\otimes t^\perp)$, $A\otimes F$ and $A\otimes F$, so a central wire returns once from $A\otimes F$ to $B\otimes F$, losing $P\otimes F$.

quote.quote: The gate order below confines all decreases to this return, while the other edges realize the prescribed stage transitions.

children.claim: Every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing $h$, so $L=Ich$; the residuals are $B\otimes t_X^\perp$ and $P\otimes t_X^\perp$ on $X$, $B\otimes t_Y^\perp$ and $P\otimes t_Y^\perp$ on $Y$, $B\otimes F$ and then $P\otimes F$ three times on a central wire, $B\otimes\langle t_Y\rangle$, $(B\otimes t_Y^\perp)\perp(P\otimes\langle t_X\rangle)$, $P\otimes\langle t_X,t_Y\rangle^\perp$ (of dimension $h-2$, using $t_X\perp t_Y$) and $P\otimes\langle t_Y\rangle$ on a side wire, $(A\otimes F)\otimes Q^\perp$ on each scratch sink edge, and zero elsewhere.

quote.quote: The only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4; their dimension loss is $h$.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb F_2$ every nonzero edge residual is nondegenerate and contains a vector of norm one, so it has an orthonormal basis, alternating planes being absorbed into a unit line through the vectors $w+a$, $w+b$, $w+a+b$.

quote.quote: For the binary label space, every nonzero orthogonal residual of an edge has an orthonormal basis.

children.claim: With $c_{\rm b}=100$ and $c_{\rm c}=101$ central wires per invocation the loss ratios are exactly $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$, both smaller than $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

adds.name: label space
adds.meaning: The ambient label space $F^{\otimes3}$ of dimension $m=h^3$, with $F=\mathbb Q^h$ for the bit network and $F=\mathbb F_2^h$ for the complex network.

adds.meaning: The indicator vector in $F$ of a three-element subset $T$ of $[h]$.

adds.meaning: The line spanned by $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$, the source label of the data role $X_a$.

children.claim: Giving each gate or sink with label $U$ the projection $P_U$ onto $U$ along $U^\perp$, the source of $X_a$ the matrix $-P_{U_a}$ and every other source zero yields rational matrices with $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ on every role and total edge rank $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}=177176569088785861287000000<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Read the rank of each edge difference $P_V-P_U$ off the label dimensions and add the exceptional source edges.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its complement, so its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$, and reversing the edge only negates the matrix.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The only exceptions are the $N$ negative source projections: at stage 1 the first gate on $X_a$ has label exactly $U_a$, so that edge's matrix is $2P_{U_a}$, of rank one although its dimension change is zero, adding $N$ to the rank sum.

quote.quote: Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: Hence $s_{\rm b}=(W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b})+N$, whose deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$ because $L_{\rm b}<N/2$.

quote.quote: Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

children.claim: For an input $X_a$ (routed to $Y_a$) the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix, so every endpoint difference is $I_m$.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: With phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{q_U(x)})H^{\otimes m}$, where $q_U(x)=\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4$, each edge's frame change is a product of one translation kernel $\frac{1+i}{2}I+\frac{1-i}{2}X_v$ or its inverse per vector of an orthonormal residual basis, these number $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}=1873807244636671267308000000<W_{\rm c}m$, and after diagonal corrections every role receives $C^{\otimes m}$.
children.method: Use additivity of Hamming weight modulo four on orthogonal binary vectors to split each phase change into one factor per residual basis vector, conjugate each factor by Hadamard matrices into a translation kernel, and repair the one non-standard endpoint with signs and a phase.

motivation.text: Orthogonal decompositions of labels make Hamming-weight phases additive, so each residual basis vector contributes one independent two-point kernel and the residual count of the labels becomes the number of smaller calls.

children.claim: Since $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)=\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)-2|\operatorname{supp}z\cap\operatorname{supp}w|$, weight is additive modulo four when $z\cdot w=0$, so for $V=U\perp E$ with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $E$ one has $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\pmod4$, negated on a decreasing edge.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each basis vector has odd weight, so its phase is $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}{2}+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}{2}(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ turns the character $(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ into the translation $X_v$, giving the kernel $\frac{1+i}{2}I+\frac{1-i}{2}X_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: By the label count the basis lengths sum to $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, whose deficit from $W_{\rm c}m$ is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

quote.quote: The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: On $k$ columns every frame and edge operator is the $k$-th tensor power of its one-column version, so each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all $k$ columns and there are still $s_{\rm c}$ factors.

quote.quote: Thus each residual vector contributes one factor acting on all $k$ columns, and there are $s_{\rm c}$ such factors over the network.

children.claim: The zero label has frame $I$ and the full label has frame $C^{\otimes m}$; on the route $X_a\to Y_a$ the operator is $C^{-1}$ on the $27$ coordinates of the support of $t_{a_1}\otimes t_{a_2}\otimes t_{a_3}$ and $C$ elsewhere, which $C=iZC^{-1}Z$ corrects by applying $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after, and negating the physical $X$ outputs and undoing the exchange leaves $C^{\otimes mk}$ on every role.

quote.quote: There are $27k$ inverse factors, so the identity $C=iZC^{-1}Z$ turns each of them into $C$.

adds.name: two-point kernel
adds.meaning: The $2\times2$ matrix $C=H\operatorname{diag}(1,i)H=\frac{1+i}{2}I+\frac{1-i}{2}X$, with $H$ the normalized Hadamard matrix and $X$ the coordinate swap.

children.claim: The relative deficits $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and since $\log m<20$, $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20\cdot2^{-50})>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: Two disjoint contiguous $u$-bit address fields of an array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ are interchanged, $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$, in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps by one fixed procedure on a fixed number of tapes.
children.method: Realize the shear $H\gets H+D$ by running the bit network on row-split role streams with shear frames, so that each edge is a matrix shear paid for by rank-many smaller interchanges; three shears give the interchange, and padding removes the width and row restrictions.

motivation.text: The sum of the edge ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, so the recurrence for the normalized cost grows by less than a factor $m$ each time the width is multiplied by $m$, which saves a power of the width.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

children.claim: For a fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$, the shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ of two groups of $m$ equal radix-$q$ fields, all $H_i$ before all $D_j$, costs exactly $a$ interchanges of an $H$ field with a $D$ field plus $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$ and a partial permutation $\Pi$ with $a$ ones, perform the triangular changes as ordered controlled shifts, and implement each one of $\Pi$ by two linear updates around a single field interchange.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts update a later field from earlier ones in linear time, and lower-triangular coordinate changes only ever update in that direction, so only the rank-many entries of $\Pi$ need a costly interchange.

quote.quote: Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix of rank $a$ factors as $E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with exactly $a$ ones, by eliminating from the topmost nonzero row at its rightmost nonzero entry (a Bruhat factorization with reversed coordinate order).

quote.quote: Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones.

children.claim: Fixing the factorizations of the finitely many matrices once, an odd prime $q$ exceeding all numerators and denominators in their table makes every identity specialize to $\mathbb Z/q^k\mathbb Z$ with the triangular factors still invertible, found by a finite computation independent of the field width.

quote.quote: For example, a prime exceeding the absolute values of all its nonzero numerators and denominators suffices.

children.claim: A lower-triangular transformation of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: coordinates are updated in descending physical order, each multiplied by its diagonal unit and shifted by a fixed combination of earlier, still original, coordinates.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: After transforming $D$ by $E_2$ and $H$ by $E_1^{-1}$, each one of $\Pi$ at $(i,j)$ is done by $D_j\gets D_j+H_i$, interchanging $(H_i,D_j)$, and $D_j\gets H_i-D_j$, which sends $(h,d)$ to $(h+d,d)$ with a single interchange, after which $H$ and $D$ are transformed back.

quote.quote: On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.

children.claim: For chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits preceded by a row field whose length is divisible by $W^k$, the interchange costs $O(Ve^\tau)$, because the cost per unit volume obeys $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$.
children.method: Split whole rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network with shear frames $\Phi_M$, implement each edge change $\Phi_{A_e}$ by $\operatorname{rank}A_e$ recursive interchanges of chunks $m$ times narrower on volume $V/W$, finish with three shears, and solve the volume-normalized recurrence.

motivation.text: An edge of rank $a$ costs $a$ smaller interchanges, so the $s<Wm$ smaller calls each on a stream of volume $V/W$ make the normalized cost grow by $s/W<m^\tau$ per factor $m$ of width.

quote.quote: An edge matrix of rank $a$ will require $a$ smaller interchanges.

children.claim: The bit network supplies the required finite contract: $W=W_{\rm b}$ wires, rational matrices common to all incidences of a gate with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ for every role, and edge differences $A_e$ whose ranks sum to $s=s_{\rm b}<Wm$.

quote.quote: supplies these conditions with $W=W_{\rm b}$ and $s=s_{\rm b}$.

children.claim: Writing each chunk as $m$ fields of $e/m$ digits (vectors $H,D$) and dealing row $Wg+(w-1)$ to role $w$ gives $W$ role streams of identical shape with the full ranges of $H$ and $D$, each of volume $V/W$ with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: The computed forward transforms have norm below $0.26$, so $z=Q_p(\widetilde U\cdot\widetilde V_1)$ has norm below $0.5$ and $\|z-U\cdot V_1\|<(2E_s+2)2^{-p}$ for $U=RF_{\boldsymbol s}u$, $V_1=RF_{\boldsymbol s}v$.

quote.quote: Thus $\|z-U\cdot V_1\|<(2E_s+2)h_p$.

children.claim: By the cancellation identity $G(U\cdot V_1)=(u*v)/S^2$ for $G=RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+$, and the computed opposite transform, legal on $z$ since $\|z\|<0.5$, errs from it by less than $(3E_s+2)2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: The computed opposite transform may be applied to $z$ because $\|z\|<.5$.

children.claim: Scaling exactly by $S$ approximates $w=(u*v)/S$ with error below $E_w2^{-p}$, $E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L$, and $\|w\|<1/16$ keeps the result in the disk.

quote.quote: This proves the disk bound for the computed first scaled result.

children.claim: Scaling exactly by $2^{2b+4}S$ gives the integer convolution with error below $2^{2b+4}S\cdot28\cdot2^\gamma T^2L\cdot2^{-6b}<448b\,2^{-b+\gamma}\le448b\,2^{-3b/4}<\frac12$, using $S\le T<2^b$, $L<b$ and $\gamma\le b/4$, so the nearest integer is the correct coefficient.

quote.quote: The strict error below $1/2$ makes the nearest integer to that value the unique correct coefficient.

children.claim: After $\Phi^{-1}$ the carries $k_{j+1}=\lfloor(c_j+k_j)/2^b\rfloor$, $k_0=0$, stay below $2^{2b}$ by induction, the invariant $\sum_{h<j}c_h2^{bh}=\sum_{h<j}d_h2^{bh}+k_j2^{bj}$ fixes the low digits $d_h$, and since the product is below $2^{2n}$ the output has exactly $2n$ bits.

quote.quote: The exact product is less than $2^{2n}$; all bits above position $2n-1$ are therefore zero.

children.claim: The whole algorithm runs in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time: divided by $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$, every cost is at most $p^{1-2\kappa}$ up to factors polylogarithmic in $p=\Theta(\log n)$.
children.method: Tabulate each operation's cost divided by $V=Tp$ as a power of $p$, compute the seven margins below one, show that setup and exceptional streams are $o(V)$, and use schoolbook multiplication below one fixed cutoff.

motivation.text: Since $p=\Theta(\log n)$, a normalized cost $p^{1-2\kappa}$ times any fixed power of $\log p$ is $O(p^{1-\kappa})$, so it suffices to bound every row's exponent with slack $2\kappa$.

quote.quote: This explicit slack will cover any remaining fixed power of $\log p$.

children.claim: With $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$ and $\Theta(p)$ bits per coefficient, the normalized costs and their powers of $p$ are: prefix-slot moves and individual butterfly rounds $dK$ ($\epsilon(1+c)$); chunk exchanges for the transform layout $pK^{\tau-1}$ ($1-\epsilon c(1-\tau)$); simultaneous butterfly rounds $\ell d^{\lambda'}$ ($1-\epsilon(1-\lambda')$); CRT and axis layouts $d^2(1+\ell^\tau)$ ($\tau+\epsilon(2-\tau)$); Gaussian line maps $dp^{1/2+\delta}\alpha$ ($3/4+\delta+3\epsilon/2$); chirps, twists and scalar products $dp^\delta$ ($\epsilon+\delta$); packed polynomial products $\log(rp)$ ($1-\epsilon$); final scaling and rounding $p^\delta$, and input, padding, carries and output $1$, both absorbed.

quote.quote: For the cost calculation put $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$.

children.claim: The seven margins below one are $g_1=1-\epsilon(1+c)>\frac12$, $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-181}$, $g_3=\epsilon(1-\lambda')=2^{-129}$, $g_4=1-\tau-\epsilon(2-\tau)>2^{-51}$, $g_5=\frac14-\delta-\frac32\epsilon>\frac18$, $g_6=1-\delta-\epsilon>\frac12$ and $g_7=\epsilon=2^{-75}$, so the smallest is $g_2=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

quote.quote: Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

children.salient: The binding margin $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)$ comes from the chunk exchanges of the transform layout, so $\kappa$ is fixed by the address-interchange exponent $\tau$.

children.claim: The first three rows are the transform cost terms: $O(dK)$ linear scans, $O(p/K)$ exchanges of $K$-bit chunks at $O(VK^\tau)$ each giving $O(pK^{\tau-1})$, and at most $\ell$ simultaneous rounds at $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ each, including basis changes, repair, padding and cleanup.

quote.quote: Its positional layout uses $O(p/K)$ exchanges of width-$K$ chunks, because $d\ell=O(p)$.

children.claim: Axis exposure and restoration use $O(d^2)$ adjacent axis moves at $O(V(1+\ell^\tau))$ each, and the $d$ CRT rotations cost $O(dV)$ with $o(Tp)$ offset setup.

quote.quote: Axis exposure and restoration require $O(d^2)$ adjacent axis moves.

children.claim: The Gaussian line maps cost $\sum_i(T/t_i)O(t_ip^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)=O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$, and dividing by $V$ with $\alpha=\Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$ gives the power $3/4+\delta+3\epsilon/2$.

quote.quote: The factor $\alpha=\Theta(p^{1/4+\epsilon/2})$ explains its displayed power of $p$.

children.claim: Chirp phases need $d$ squares and products per entry by the established multiplier plus one exponential, $O(dp^{1+\delta})$ per entry, and the twists and scalar pointwise products fit the same row.

quote.quote: then generating the exponentials, costs $O(dp^{1+\delta})$ per entry.

children.claim: The two products by $S$ cost $O(p\log p)$ per entry, normalized $O(p^\delta)$, and the $T/r$ records of each ring product need four integer products on $O(rp)=o(n)$ bits, $O(Tp\log(rp))$ in total, using the established multiplier as an ordinary subroutine and never the improved algorithm.

quote.quote: they do not call the improved algorithm being constructed.

children.claim: Setup at the $p^{O(1)}$ recursion visits, per-record address work over records of superpolynomial length $r$, per-line Gaussian setup, and the compact exceptional streams of packed additions, $O(Vp^{A'}2^{-K})$, all cost $o(V)$ in the worst case, and no step rescans parked ancestors.

quote.quote: This is a deterministic worst-case bound.

children.claim: Every row's power is at most $1-2\kappa$ and any fixed power of $\log p$ is eventually below $p^\kappa$, so the time is $O(Tp\,p^{1-\kappa})=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$, and schoolbook multiplication below one fixed cutoff extends the bound to every $n$.

quote.quote: Any fixed power of $\log p$ is at most $p^\kappa$ eventually.

children.salient: Seven very different costs all land strictly below $p^1$, and the smallest margin, $2^{-181}$, is exactly twice $\kappa$.

adds.name: input length
adds.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers multiplied.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ by which the running time beats $n\lg n$, half the smallest margin $2^{-181}$ of the cost table.

adds.name: logical volume
adds.meaning: The number of stored data bits of the array being processed; for the full padded array $V=Tp=\Theta(n)$.

adds.name: digit width
adds.meaning: The number $b=\lceil\log_2n\rceil$ of bits in one radix-$2^b$ digit of the inputs.

adds.name: working precision
adds.meaning: The number $p=6b$ of fractional bits of every fixed-point coefficient.

adds.name: number of axes
adds.meaning: The number $d=\lfloor b^\epsilon\rfloor=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ of transform axes, which also bounds the chunks a butterfly layer selects.

adds.name: chunk width
adds.meaning: The number $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$ of address bits in one chunk of the transform layout.

adds.name: record length
adds.meaning: The number $r=2^{\lceil(\log_2T)/d\rceil}=2^{\Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})}$ of complex coefficients in one polynomial record of $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$.

adds.name: record exponent
adds.meaning: The exponent $\ell=\log_2r=\Theta(p^{1-\epsilon})$, the number of radix-two levels of an axis of length $r$.

adds.name: padded box size
adds.meaning: The number of entries of the padded power-of-two box, the power of two in $[4n/b,8n/b)$.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ of the address-interchange cost $O(Vu^\tau)$.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\lambda'=1-2^{-54}$ of the butterfly-layer cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.

adds.name: axis exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $\epsilon=2^{-75}$ with $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$.

adds.name: chunk exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $c=2^{-56}$ with $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$.

root.salient: The bound beats the conjectured optimum $n\log n$ by the factor $(\lg n)^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$: tiny, but a genuine power of the logarithm, valid for every input length.
